1. (Currently amended) A battery assembly comprising: an enclosure; a first battery cell positioned within the enclosure; and a first sensor positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, wherein the first sensor is configured to detect at least one force influencing the first battery cell by varying conductance based on mechanical stress applied to the first sensor.

2. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising an adhesive layer positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, and wherein the adhesive layer is configured to maintain the first sensor in contact with at least one of the first battery cell and the enclosure.

3. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 2, wherein at least a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned adjacent at least a portion the first sensor in a plane between the first battery cell and the enclosure, and wherein the adhesive layer does not completely encapsulate the first sensor.

4. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 3, wherein the adhesive layer extends around at least a portion of the first sensor in the plane while leaving at least one surface of the first sensor exposed to detect forces.

5. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 2, wherein a portion of the first sensor extends through a gap in the adhesive layer towards an edge of the first battery cell, and wherein the exposed portion of the first sensor is configured to detect deformation of the first battery cell.

6. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 2, wherein a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned between the first sensor and one of the first battery cell and the enclosure.

7. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising a deformable element positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the enclosure, and wherein the deformable element is configured to transmit forces to the first sensor.

8. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1, wherein: the enclosure comprises an enclosure portion of protective film; the first sensor is positioned between first battery cell and the enclosure portion; and the protective film is configured to allow force transmission to the first sensor.

9. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 8, wherein the protective film is a polyester film having a thickness configured to transmit mechanical forces to the first sensor.

10. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1, wherein: the enclosure comprises a plastic case portion; the first sensor is positioned between first battery cell and the plastic case portion; and the plastic case portion is configured to allow force transmission to the first sensor.

11. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising a second battery cell stacked on top of the first battery cell, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the second battery cell, and wherein the first sensor is configured to detect forces transmitted through the second battery cell to the first battery cell.

12. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 11 further comprising an adhesive layer between the first battery cell and the second battery cell, wherein the adhesive layer is configured to maintain the first sensor in contact with at least one of the first battery cell and the second battery cell.

13. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 12, wherein at least a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned adjacent at least a portion the first sensor in a plane between the first battery cell and the second battery cell, and wherein the adhesive layer does not completely encapsulate the first sensor.

14. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 13, wherein the adhesive layer extends around at least a portion of the first sensor in the plane while leaving at least one surface of the first sensor exposed to detect forces.

15. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 12, wherein a portion of the first sensor extends through a gap in the adhesive layer towards an edge of the first battery cell, and wherein the exposed portion of the first sensor is configured to detect deformation of the first battery cell.

16. (Previously presented) The battery assembly of claim 12, wherein a portion of the adhesive layer is positioned between the first sensor and one of the first battery cell and the second battery cell.

17. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1 further comprising: a second battery cell stacked on top of the first battery cell, wherein the first sensor is positioned between the first battery cell and the second battery cell; a third battery cell stacked on top of the second battery cell; and a second sensor positioned between the third battery cell and the second battery cell for detecting at least one force influencing the third battery cell, wherein each of the first and second sensors is configured to vary conductance based on mechanical stress applied to the respective sensor.

18. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 17 further comprising a processor configured to: receive a first sensor output signal from the first sensor based on conductance variation of the first sensor; receive a second sensor output signal from the second sensor based on conductance variation of the second sensor; conduct an evaluation based at least on the received output signals; and generate at least one processor output signal based on the evaluation.

19. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 18, wherein the processor is further configured to alter an operation of the third battery cell independently from an operation of the first battery cell based on the at least one processor output signal, wherein the alteration is responsive to force detection by the second sensor.

20. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 18, wherein the processor is further configured to turn off the third battery cell and to maintain operation of the first battery cell based on the at least one processor output signal, wherein the turn-off decision is based on force detection by the second sensor indicating mechanical stress on the third battery cell.

21. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 1, wherein the first sensor comprises: force sensing material having a conductance that is configured to vary based on at least one force influencing the first battery cell, wherein the conductance variation is responsive to mechanical stress; and force sensing circuitry coupled to the force sensing material, wherein the force sensing circuitry is configured to produce a force output signal based on the conductance of the force sensing material.

22. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 21, wherein the force sensing material comprises at least one variable electrical conductor configured to change conductance in response to mechanical deformation.

23. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 22, wherein the at least one variable electrical conductor has a first level of electrical conductance when the at least one variable electrical conductor is quiescent, and wherein the at least one variable electrical conductor has a second level of conductance when a mechanical stress is applied to the at least one variable electrical conductor, wherein the second level is distinguishably different from the first level.

24. (Currently amended) The battery assembly of claim 22, wherein the at least one variable electrical conductor is a quantum tunneling composite configured to exhibit conductance variation in response to compression or deformation.
